messages.text: England unchanged for World Cup clash vs France with Lewis absent again

metadata.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis absent again as England unchanged for clash vs France despite opening defeat | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis absent again as England unchanged for clash vs France despite opening defeat England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am kick-off BST) for second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; England play Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on October 30; England Women began their campaign with big win vs Wales in Perth Tuesday 20 October 2026 07:48, UK Image: Mikey Lewis will not feature for England again as England opt for unchanged squad England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France. AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening game against Tonga. Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while there also remains no place in the squad for Mikey Lewis. As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on. messages.text: Reese scores 30 points as Atlanta win at Golden State to level WNBA Finals

metadata.summary: Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1.
metadata.content: WNBA Finals: Angel Reese scores 30 points, 16 rebounds as Atlanta Dream win at Golden State Valkyries to level best-of-seven series 1-1 | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WNBA Finals: Angel Reese scores 30 points, 16 rebounds as Atlanta Dream win at Golden State Valkyries to level best-of-seven series 1-1 Atlanta Dream level WNBA Finals at 1-1 in best-of-seven series as they secure 79-65 away win at Golden State Valkyries; Angel Reese proves star with 30 points and 16 rebounds - third player ever to register such stats in a Finals game; watch WNBA Finals live on Sky Sports Tuesday 20 October 2026 07:10, UK Image: Angel Reese proved the standout as the Atlanta Dream levelled the WNBA Finals 1-1 vs Golden State Valkyries Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1. In front of the Valkyries' raucous home crowd, the Atlanta star had no choice but to raise her voice - and Reese knew she had to raise her game, too. "For me, I think I let my team down last game not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," Reese said. "Not even just about scoring, my screen quality, me hustling and running to get rebounds, just doing the things that they know me to do. metadata.summary: James Maddison says he has "so much more to give" Tottenham after he marked his first start in nearly 18 months with a stunning goal that helped Spurs to their first Premier League win of the season.
metadata.content: James Maddison marks first Tottenham start in nearly 18 months with stunning goal in first Premier League win of season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content James Maddison marks first Tottenham start in nearly 18 months with stunning goal in first Premier League win of season Tottenham playmaker struck opener in 3-1 win over Coventry which moved side off foot of Premier League; the 29-year-old was making his first start following torrid long lay-off after suffering an ACL injury Tuesday 20 October 2026 06:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In his first competitive start for Tottenham since their 2024-25 Europa League semi-final, James Maddison puts Spurs ahead early in their Premier League clash with Coventry. James Maddison says he has "so much more to give" Tottenham after he marked his first start in nearly 18 months with a stunning goal that helped Spurs to their first Premier League win of the season. The playmaker was influential in the 3-1 victory over Coventry in north London , opening the scoring with a curling strike from range to set Roberto De Zerbi's side on their way to a much-needed win which moves them off the foot of the table. The 29-year-old, who has two years to run on his Spurs contract, first came back toward the end of last season after recovering from his ACL injury but has faced numerous setbacks that have delayed his full return until now. messages.text: Ronaldo punished over Portugal walkout with fine he can pay off in 39 seconds

metadata.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days and fined £215 over his walkout from the Portugal national team following an explosive fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus.
metadata.content: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal captain punished over walkout following explosive row with head coach Jorge Jesus | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal captain punished over walkout following explosive row with head coach Jorge Jesus Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo claimed head coach Jorge Jesus twice broke his word about the star's role in the team after he walked out on the national team's camp on the eve of a match; he has now been punished for his actions but will not miss any Portugal matches Monday 19 October 2026 20:37, UK Image: Cristiano Ronaldo has made 234 appearances for Portugal Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days and fined £215 over his walkout from the Portugal national team following an explosive fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus. The Portuguese FA's disciplinary council did not specify when Ronaldo's ban begins, but Sky Sports News understands it is enforced from the date he left the squad's training camp in Denmark on September 30. It means the 41-year-old former Manchester United and Real Madrid star is available to play in Portugal's Nations League matches next month against Denmark and Wales if he is called upon by Jesus. Ronaldo accused Jesus of broken promises and a "breach of trust" over his involvement in the team . The new head coach denied there had been any agreement.
